# makereel — full description (for people and AI assistants)

Source: https://github.com/simarpreetsingh-019/makereel · Website: https://simarpreetsingh-019.github.io/makereel/

## In one paragraph

makereel is a free, open-source application that turns live streams and long videos into short, captioned
vertical reels (9:16) for YouTube Shorts, Instagram Reels and TikTok. It runs entirely on the user's own
computer (Windows 10/11, macOS, Linux) and opens in the browser at http://localhost:8765. It can clip a
YouTube, Twitch or Kick stream while it is live, watch channels 24/7 and clip them automatically, and
process past streams, ordinary videos (any site yt-dlp supports) and local files. Moments are found from
loudness and live-chat activity, optionally ranked by an AI judge. Each reel gets word-by-word captions,
automatic framing (split screen, follow the speaker, or blurred background), the creator's channel badge,
and post text that credits the creator with a link to the exact moment. No account, server or API key is
required; nothing is uploaded.

## Who it is for

- Clippers and editors who turn streamers' broadcasts into shorts.
- Streamers and podcasters repurposing their own streams and videos.
- Especially Indian (Hindi / Hinglish) and English gaming and talk streams.

## What makes it different

Compared with SupoClip, OpusClip, OpenShorts, Clips Kitty and Cutawan:
1. Clips live streams while they are live (rolling buffer), not only finished videos.
2. Watches channels 24/7: clips them when they go live, and new uploads and premieres.
3. Finds moments from chat activity and loudness, not only the transcript.
4. Credits the original creator on every reel (badge) and in every post text.
5. Local-first and free: no cloud, no account, no API key; optional AI uses the user's own key or a local model.
6. Strong Hindi/English/Hinglish captions: language per sentence, a Hinglish speech model, YouTube's own
   captions for finished videos, and a second model that double-checks captions.

## How it works

1. yt-dlp asks the platform where the stream is (HLS playlist links).
2. ffmpeg copies the stream without re-encoding into 6-second pieces in a rolling 10-minute buffer, and
   decodes the audio to measure loudness every second. A second yt-dlp process counts live-chat messages.
3. A jump in loudness or chat opens a moment; it stays open while the moment lasts and closes after about
   8 calm seconds. Reels are 30 seconds to several minutes, within the user's limits (max 5 minutes).
4. The moment is cut, transcribed (faster-whisper / CTranslate2; or YouTube's own captions for finished
   videos), double-checked by a second speech model, framed (YuNet face detection, mouth-movement speaker
   tracking) and rendered with a hardware video encoder when available.
5. Post text with credits is written next to each reel. Everything stays on the computer.

## Features

Finding moments: live clipping; chat replay for past streams; automatic reel length; reels-per-hour limit;
optional AI judge (local model via Ollama/LM Studio, Claude, or any OpenAI-compatible API) with hook,
engagement, value and shareability scores and titles; one recording per stream.

Captions: word-by-word, 7 styles, safe zones for app buttons; Whisper models (base, small, medium,
distil-large-v3, large-v3) and Hinglish models (Oriserve Hindi2Hinglish Apex and Swift); language per
sentence; original script, English letters, or English translation; YouTube's own captions for finished
YouTube videos (original-speech tracks only); second-model double-check with a side-by-side view where
disagreements are highlighted in yellow; edit words with timing kept; shift or tap-to-sync; SRT/VTT import.

Framing and look: auto layout (split screen for two people or webcam over gameplay, follow the speaker,
blurred fill, crop, black bars); speaker tracking by mouth movement; editable camera cuts; "show everyone"
zoom-outs; brand kit (logo, fonts, colours); creator badge.

Editing and export: trim, split, join, make short versions of a long reel; quote and note cards, outros;
export 9:16, 4:5, 1:1, 16:9.

Automation: 24/7 channel watcher (live streams, new uploads, premieres) with start-date window and check
interval; inbox file; daemon mode; local REST API.

Setup and computer: one-command installers (they install ffmpeg, Node.js and a private Python via uv);
speech models suggested for the computer (RAM, disk, NVIDIA GPU); NVIDIA GPU speech with automatic CPU
fallback; processing modes (cool and quiet / balanced / fast); live CPU and Mac temperature card; choose
where files are saved; clear cache; in-app updates verified by checksum; commands `makereel start`,
`status`, `help`, `update`, `gpu`, `signin`.

YouTube bot checks ("Sign in to confirm you're not a bot"): retries other YouTube clients first, then
uses the user's sign-in (a cookies file, or a browser such as Firefox); notifies the user when blocked.

## Install

Windows (PowerShell):
    irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/simarpreetsingh-019/makereel/main/install.ps1 | iex
macOS / Linux (Terminal):
    curl -LsSf https://raw.githubusercontent.com/simarpreetsingh-019/makereel/main/install.sh | bash
Then: `makereel start`. Update: `makereel update`.

Download size: about 90 MB of libraries plus a speech model (150 MB to 3 GB, chosen during setup).

## Requirements

Windows 10/11, macOS or Linux; 4 GB RAM minimum, 8–16 GB recommended; an NVIDIA GPU is optional.

## Limits

- YouTube's automatic captions are available only after a live stream ends.
- On Windows, Chrome/Brave/Edge logins can't be read by other apps (app-bound encryption); use Firefox or a
  sign-in file if YouTube asks to confirm you're not a bot.
- Live clipping needs makereel running; 24/7 watching needs the computer on.
- Reposting requires the right to do so; credit is not permission.

## FAQ

Is makereel free? Yes, it runs locally with nothing to pay for.
Does it upload videos? No.
Which platforms? YouTube, Twitch, Kick, any site yt-dlp supports, and local files.
Does it need a GPU? No; an NVIDIA GPU makes speech faster.
Does it support Hindi? Yes, including mixed Hindi-English (Hinglish).
Is it open source? The code is public on GitHub.
